items.headline: Texans hammer the Colts 26-3 on Thursday night
items.body: C.J. Stroud threw three touchdown passes and Houston's defense smothered Indianapolis in a 26-3 Thursday Night Football rout. David Montgomery bulldozed for 107 rushing yards and Will Anderson Jr. even added a safety, as the Texans grabbed a grip on the AFC South.
items.say: Texans just rolled the Colts 26-3 on Thursday night — Stroud threw three touchdowns and the defense was all over them. You following any football this year?

items.headline: Dame goes off — Lillard drops 33 as the Blazers win in Milwaukee
items.body: Damian Lillard poured in 33 points with five made threes and Scoot Henderson chipped in 27 as Portland knocked off the Bucks 124-114 on the road. Classic Dame, pulling up from the logo like it's a layup line.
items.say: Damian Lillard dropped 33 on the Bucks last night — still shooting from the logo like it's nothing. You catching any NBA this season?

items.headline: Cutter Gauthier just did something no NHL player ever has
items.body: Anaheim's 22-year-old Cutter Gauthier became the first player in NHL history to record four hat tricks in a single calendar month, capping a ridiculous November that also featured a 10-game goal streak. The Ducks have suddenly turned into appointment viewing.
items.say: There's a kid in Anaheim, Cutter Gauthier, who just became the first player ever with four hat tricks in one month — nobody in NHL history had done that. You follow any hockey?

items.headline: Prochazka headlines UFC Qatar on Saturday
items.body: The UFC touches down in Doha on Saturday with a light-heavyweight scrap: fan-favorite wild man Jiri Prochazka takes on unbeaten rising star Navajo Stirling, with former champ Aljamain Sterling in the co-main event. Prochazka fights are many things, but boring is never one of them.
items.say: Fun UFC card out of Qatar on Saturday — Jiri Prochazka's headlining, and that guy throws spinning everything. His knockouts are wild. You ever watch the fights?

items.headline: Big Saturday in the Prem — Newcastle host Arsenal in a title-race test
items.body: The weekend's standout fixture sends title-chasing Arsenal to a roaring St James' Park to face Newcastle on Saturday evening. Then Sunday delivers Liverpool vs Manchester United at Anfield — Mauricio Pochettino's very first match in the United dugout.
items.say: Arsenal are at Newcastle on Saturday in a big one for the title race, and then Pochettino makes his Man United debut at Anfield on Sunday. Loaded weekend. You follow the Premier League?

items.headline: Brad Pitt's Cliff Booth is back — Fincher's trailer is here
items.body: David Fincher directs a Quentin Tarantino-penned follow-up to 'Once Upon a Time in Hollywood,' with Brad Pitt reprising his Oscar-winning stuntman Cliff Booth. 'The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth' plays IMAX for a two-week run starting November 25 before hitting Netflix December 23.
items.say: There's a sequel to Once Upon a Time in Hollywood coming — Brad Pitt's back as the stuntman, and David Fincher directed it. The trailer looks so slick. You a Tarantino guy?

items.headline: Take That are back — new album 'Dreamers' drops today
items.body: The British pop institution releases their 10th studio album, 'Dreamers,' today — three decades on from 'Back for Good' and still filling arenas. A perfect excuse to cue up the big singalongs.
items.say: Take That put out a new album today — the 'Back for Good' guys, if you go back that far. Those songs are ridiculously catchy. You remember them?

items.headline: Netflix opens the televangelist vault — 'Primetime Preacher$' is streaming now
items.body: Acclaimed true-crime documentarian Joe Berlinger digs into the 1980s golden age of TV preachers — the rise and spectacular crash of empires like Jim and Tammy Faye Bakker's. Stranger-than-fiction stuff, out today on Netflix.
items.say: New Netflix doc about those '80s TV preachers — the whole Jim and Tammy Faye Bakker saga. That stuff is wild. You into true-crime documentaries?

items.headline: Creed's 'Weathered' turns 25 — and the band's having a real moment again
items.body: Riding a genuine nostalgia comeback, Creed reissued their diamond-selling 2001 album 'Weathered' today as a newly remastered 25th-anniversary deluxe, complete with bonus tracks and a cover of The Doors' 'Riders on the Storm.' 'My Sacrifice' and 'One Last Breath' live here.
items.say: Creed are having a real moment again — they just dropped a 25th-anniversary edition of 'Weathered.' Those songs were everywhere in the early 2000s. Secret Creed fan? Everybody kind of is.
